Stable controller identities and compact movie columns

button_layout.Rd

Without a movie, returns the fixed gamepad and peripheral registry. With a movie, returns only its controller's columns, in matrix order. column is a local matrix index; id and key identify the same control across recordings. Unpressed controls supported by the controller are retained. Matrices omit registry entries outside that controller's layout. The registry contains 53 consecutive IDs. Keypad digits and equally numbered Power Pad sensors share numbered_0 through numbered_12 (IDs 40-52), with kind numbered. Microphone is ID 53. Serial positions in a BK2 LogKey are decoded independently of those sensor numbers.

Usage

button_layout(movie = NULL)

Arguments

movie

An imported recording, or NULL for the fixed registry.

Value

Data frame with column, id, key, mnemonic, name and kind.

Details

Additional named controls, such as keyboard keys, have character IDs of the form control:<key>. These are stable within their source key namespace. They appear in the movie's layout without expanding unrelated controllers. Equivalent device buttons share registered IDs: Wii Home and libTAS Guide use Mode (19), Wii 1/2 use X/Y (9/10), and light-gun triggers use A (8). Arcade Attack/Punch use A, Jump and Doom Use use B, Kick uses X, and D uses Y. Mouse left/right/middle use A/B/X, and buttons 4/5 use L1/R1. GunCon trigger, side A, side B, and offscreen shot use A/B/X/Y. Keypad Enter/Clear use Start/Select; Star/Pound retain qualified source IDs. Device-qualified openMSX controls also remain distinct because multiple devices can occupy the same input stream. A shared ID groups comparable controller roles; game actions can differ. When aliases are present, source_inputs retains the decoded input array and source_layout identifies its columns and their universal_key mapping. If several source buttons map to one ID, that column is active whenever any of them is pressed. Registered controls use fixed numeric IDs; a mixed layout represents all IDs as character strings. Use keys or IDs for matching, rather than coercing the complete ID column to integers. Source keyboard code sets remain distinct.

Examples

path <- system.file("extdata", "sample.m64", package = "replayr")
button_layout(read_movie(path))
#>    column id        key mnemonic    name   kind
#> 1       1  1 dpad_right        R   Right button
#> 2       2  2  dpad_left        L    Left button
#> 3       3  3  dpad_down        D    Down button
#> 4       4  4    dpad_up        U      Up button
#> 5       5  5      start        T   Start button
#> 6       6  7          b        B       B button
#> 7       7  8          a        A       A button
#> 8       8 11         l1        p      L1 button
#> 9       9 12         r1        q      R1 button
#> 10     10 18          z        Z       Z button
#> 11     11 20    c_right        > C-Right button
#> 12     12 21     c_left        <  C-Left button
#> 13     13 22     c_down        v  C-Down button
#> 14     14 23       c_up        ^    C-Up button
